text_blocks.snippet: Scammers in Central Illinois frequently target residents using fake text messages, phony government notices, and deceptive door-to-door repair services. Popular schemes include texts impersonating the Illinois Secretary of State or delivery carriers, local utility or city department billing imposters, and fly-by-night contractors exploiting storm damage.

list.snippet: Fake Government & DMV Texts: Scammers send text messages claiming you owe unpaid toll or traffic fines, or that your driver's license will be suspended unless you click a link.
City and Utility Imposters: Fraudsters send fake invoices or notices using forged local municipal or zoning letterheads to demand immediate payment.
Package Delivery Texts: Phishing texts pretend to be from UPS or USPS asking for credit card data or personal details to redeliver a fake package.
Storm and Home Repair Fraud: Door-to-door contractors offer "free inspections" or cheap rapid fixes after severe weather, demanding large cash down payments and leaving work unfinished.
Rental and Real Estate Fraud: Fake listings target students and movers with stolen property photos to collect upfront deposits and fake application fees.
Do not click links in unsolicited text messages or emails regarding traffic tickets, tolls, or package deliveries.
Verify bills independently by looking up official phone numbers for local cities, utilities, or agencies rather than using contact numbers on suspicious notices.
Reject cash-only deals and avoid paying full price upfront for any home repair or contractor work.

Check official portals or contact the Illinois Attorney General Consumer Fraud Bureau
or the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois if you suspect a scam.

references.title: 🚨EMAIL SCAM ALERT🚨 The Massachusetts State Police - Commonwealth Fusion Center is seeing an increase in highly convincing scam emails impersonating local permitting and zoning offices. These messages use real staff names, official-looking logos, and detailed invoices to trick applicants into sending fraudulent payments.
